intro: St. Paul write this Epistle to his BELOVED TIMOTHY, being then bishop of Ephesus, to instruct him in the duties of a bishop, both in respect to himself and to his charge; and that he ought to be well informed of the good morals of those on whom he was to impose hands: Impose not hands lightly upon any man. He tells him also how he should behave towards his clergy. The Epistle was written about 33 years after our Lord's Ascension; but where it was written is uncertain: the more general opinion is, that it was in Macedonia.

chapters.1: He puts Timothy in mind of his charge and blesses God for the mercy he himself had received.
chapters.2: Prayers are to be said for all men, because God wills the salvation of all. Women are not to teach.
chapters.3: What sort of men are to be admitted into the clergy. The church is the pillar of truth.
chapters.4: He warns him against heretics, and exhorts him to the exercise of piety.
chapters.5: He gives him lessons concerning widows, and how he is to behave to his clergy.
chapters.6: Duties of servants. The danger of covetousness. Lessons for the rich.

notes: The law is not... He means, that the just man doth good, and avoideth evil, not as compelled by the law, and merely for fear of the punishment appointed for transgressors; but voluntarily, and out of the love of God and virtue; and would do so, though there were no law.
One mediator... Christ is the one and only mediator of redemption, who gave himself, as the apostle writes in the following verse.

Of one wife.... The meaning is not that every bishop should have a wife (for St. Paul himself had none), but that no one should be admitted to the holy orders of bishop, priest, or deacon, who had been married more than once.
A neophyte.... That is, one lately baptized, a young convert.
The pillar and ground of the truth.... Therefore the church of the living God can never uphold error, nor bring in corruptions, superstition, or idolatry.

Forbidding to marry, to abstain from meats.... He speaks of the Gnostics, the Marcionites, the Eneratites, the Manicheans, and other ancient heretics, who absolutely condemned marriage, and the use of all kind of meat; because they pretended that all flesh was from an evil principle. Whereas the church of God, so far from condemning marriage, holds it a holy sacrament; and forbids it to none but such as by vow have chosen the better part: and prohibits not the use of any meats whatsoever in proper times and seasons; though she does not judge all kind of diet proper for days of fasting and penance.
Their first faith.... Their vow, by which they had engaged themselves to Christ.
